claim: FDA approved donor-islet therapy for a narrow adult T1D population with recurrent severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management
population_or_model: Adults with T1D and recurrent severe hypoglycemia
design: Regulatory approval and supporting clinical studies
endpoint: FDA indication; glycemic control and severe hypoglycemia
follow_up: Per label and primary reports
cointerventions: Allogeneic islet infusion; immunosuppression required
limitations: Narrow selected indication; donor supply, invasive procedure, immunosuppression risks; not general cure
notes: Use label and primary reports for exact efficacy denominator and adverse-event rates

claim: In the phase 1-2 zimislecel study, 10 of 12 full-dose recipients were insulin-independent at day 365
population_or_model: Selected people with T1D and impaired hypoglycemic awareness/severe hypoglycemia
endpoint: Insulin independence at day 365 (secondary outcome)
follow_up: At least 12 months; insulin independence assessed at day 365
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small and short-term; selected cohort; interim analyses were not prespecified; insulin independence does not establish cure or freedom from immunosuppression
notes: The 14-person analysis included 2 part A participants and 12 full-dose participants in parts B/C; all analyses were interim and not prespecified. The published part C primary endpoint is recorded separately in EV-008.

claim: Serious neutropenia occurred in 3 of 14 participants in the zimislecel study
population_or_model: 14 participants in the phase 1-2 study who completed at least 12 months follow-up
endpoint: Serious adverse event of neutropenia
follow_up: Study follow-up; 14 participants completed at least 12 months
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small cohort; the observed event count does not establish causation
notes: 3/14 participants had serious neutropenia; reported as the most common serious adverse event

claim: Two of 14 participants died during zimislecel study follow-up: one caused by cryptococcal meningitis and one due to progression of preexisting neurocognitive impairment
population_or_model: 14 participants in the phase 1-2 study who completed at least 12 months follow-up
endpoint: Deaths and reported causes
follow_up: Study follow-up; 14 participants completed at least 12 months
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Two deaths were observed in a small cohort; event occurrence and reported cause do not establish treatment causality
notes: The paper reported 2/14 deaths during follow-up: one caused by cryptococcal meningitis and one due to severe dementia with agitation associated with progression of preexisting neurocognitive impairment

claim: At 14 months, a single recipient of gene-edited donor islets had continued graft function without immunosuppression; insulin independence was not demonstrated
population_or_model: One person with longstanding T1D
endpoint: Graft survival/function and immune response
follow_up: 14 months
cointerventions: Gene-edited allogeneic islets; no immunosuppressive drugs
limitations: One participant; exploratory endpoint; continued graft function does not establish insulin independence, efficacy, or population safety
notes: The 2026 NEJM report follows the same single recipient reported in 2025

claim: Vertex reported that VX-264 did not meet its efficacy endpoint in phase 1-2 and would not advance further in clinical development
population_or_model: People with T1D in the VX-264 phase 1-2 study
endpoint: Efficacy endpoint and development decision
follow_up: Company update dated 2025-03-28
cointerventions: Encapsulated allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; device intended to avoid immunosuppression
limitations: Sponsor announcement; analyzed denominator and endpoint-level outcome counts were not reported in the cited update; it does not establish the biological reason for insufficient efficacy
notes: Company said additional analyses were planned; analyzed denominator and detailed results were not provided; mechanism of failure remains unresolved from these sources

claim: FDA accelerated approval allows teplizumab to delay decline in endogenous insulin production in certain 8-17 year-olds with recently diagnosed stage 3 T1D
population_or_model: Pediatric patients age 8-17 with recent stage 3 T1D
design: Adequate and well-controlled trial; accelerated approval
endpoint: C-peptide surrogate endpoint; postapproval study required
follow_up: Per trial and regulatory documents
cointerventions: Anti-CD3 antibody; prescribed monitored course
limitations: Delay/preservation is not cure; surrogate endpoint; boxed warning for viral reactivation
notes: Separate from stage 2 onset-delay indication

claim: All 12 participants in full-dose zimislecel parts B/C were free of severe hypoglycemic events during days 90-365 and had HbA1c below 7%
population_or_model: Selected people with T1D and impaired hypoglycemic awareness/severe hypoglycemia
design: Interim phase 1-2 analysis of full-dose parts B/C
endpoint: Part C primary endpoint: freedom from severe hypoglycemic events and glycemic threshold
follow_up: Severe hypoglycemic events: days 90-365; abstract does not explicitly establish the assessment time for the reported HbA1c below 7% finding
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small selected cohort; analyses were interim and not prespecified; the endpoint definition specified HbA1c below 7% or a decrease of at least 1 percentage point from baseline at one or more assessments between days 180 and 365, but the abstract does not explicitly connect the reported 12/12 HbA1c result to that window
notes: The abstract reports 12/12 participants were free of severe hypoglycemic events and had HbA1c below 7%; the endpoint-definition window is not asserted as the observed HbA1c result's timing. Do not conflate with the 14-person safety population.

claim: All 12 full-dose zimislecel participants spent more than 70% of time in the glucose target range of 70-180 mg/dL
population_or_model: Selected people with T1D and impaired hypoglycemic awareness/severe hypoglycemia
design: Interim phase 1-2 analysis of full-dose parts B/C
endpoint: Time in target glucose range
follow_up: During follow-up through day 365; the abstract does not separately specify the time-in-range aggregation interval
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small selected cohort; interim analyses were not prespecified; exact aggregation interval for this time-in-range measure is not stated in the abstract
notes: The abstract reports more than 70% time in range for the 12 full-dose participants; the reporting interval is not separately specified

claim: All 14 zimislecel-study participants had detectable C-peptide after infusion, having had undetectable C-peptide at baseline
population_or_model: 14 participants in the phase 1-2 study who completed at least 12 months follow-up
endpoint: Serum C-peptide detection during a 4-hour mixed-meal tolerance test to assess engraftment and islet function
follow_up: Baseline undetectable; post-infusion detection (exact post-infusion assessment time not specified in abstract)
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived islets; glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive therapy
limitations: Small cohort; C-peptide detection is evidence of graft function, not insulin independence or cure; exact assessment time is not stated in the abstract
notes: All 14 participants had undetectable baseline C-peptide and detectable C-peptide after zimislecel infusion; the abstract does not specify a single post-infusion time point

claim: In diabetic allogeneic humanized mice, human iPSC-derived hypoimmune islet grafts survived to day 28 and reduced fasting glucose toward 200 mg/dL
population_or_model: Diabetic allogeneic humanized NSG-SGM3 mice
endpoint: Islet graft survival and fasting glucose response
follow_up: Through day 28 after intramuscular transplantation
cointerventions: No immunosuppression reported in this model
limitations: Animal model; the paper reports eight HIP-islet recipients and individual graft/glucose trajectories, but the responder numerator is not reported; this does not establish human efficacy or cure
notes: The primary report also describes rhesus-derived HIP iPSCs in four macaques and edited primary rhesus islets in one macaque; those are separate models and are not pooled with the mouse sample.

claim: Edited primary rhesus islets survived for 40 weeks in one allogeneic immunocompetent macaque without immunosuppression
population_or_model: One allogeneic rhesus macaque recipient of hypoimmune primary islets
design: Preclinical single-animal transplant with bioluminescence and immune monitoring
endpoint: Graft survival and immune response
follow_up: 40 weeks
cointerventions: No immunosuppression
limitations: Single-animal proof-of-concept; graft persistence is not evidence of human insulin independence or long-term safety
notes: The control unedited islets in a separate recipient were rejected within one week; findings do not establish population-level effectiveness.

claim: One diabetic immunocompetent non-human primate achieved insulin independence after allogeneic transplantation of hypoimmune pseudo-islets without immunosuppression
population_or_model: One diabetic fully immunocompetent non-human primate
endpoint: Insulin independence and endocrine graft function
follow_up: Follow-up duration not stated in the accessible abstract
cointerventions: No immunosuppression
limitations: Single-animal proof-of-concept; follow-up duration and generalizability are not established by the accessible abstract; authors report Sana employment, stock, and patent interests
notes: The article title and abstract describe insulin independence; do not treat this as human clinical evidence.

claim: Six of 17 participants in the VC-02 open-device study had positive C-peptide, detected as early as six months after implant
population_or_model: People with long-standing T1D and undetectable baseline C-peptide
endpoint: Detectable C-peptide after implantation of PEC-01 cells in a vascularized open device
follow_up: As early as six months; report includes one-year data
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived pancreatic endoderm in a perforated device with systemic immunosuppression
limitations: Small uncontrolled cohort; C-peptide positivity is not insulin independence; study uses vascular ingrowth rather than immune isolation; related reports share NCT03163511
notes: Six of 17 were C-peptide positive; 63% of explanted VC-02 units showed engraftment and insulin expression at 3-12 months, a device-unit rather than participant denominator.

claim: Three of 10 participants in an optimized PEC-Direct study group achieved meal-stimulated C-peptide of at least 0.1 nmol/L from month six onwards
population_or_model: People with T1D and undetectable baseline C-peptide in an optimized-device study group
design: Interim open-label phase 1/2 report with one-year follow-up
endpoint: MMTT-stimulated C-peptide >=0.1 nmol/L
follow_up: Month 6 through month 12
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived pancreatic endoderm in a perforated open device; anti-thymocyte globulin induction with tacrolimus and mycophenolate maintenance
limitations: Small uncontrolled study; results were in a defined study group within NCT03163511; no insulin independence; one participant's GLP-1 receptor agonist use is a potential confounder for metabolic outcomes
notes: The paper reports three such responders with improved CGM measures and reduced insulin dosing; the highest time-in-range rose from 55% to 85% in one participant, while beta-cell mass in that participant's sentinel device was 4% of initial mass at month 6.

claim: Two of 10 participants in the optimized PEC-Direct report experienced treatment-emergent serious adverse events, one attributed to surgery and one to immunosuppression
population_or_model: Ten participants in the optimized PEC-Direct study group
endpoint: Treatment-emergent serious adverse events
follow_up: Through one-year follow-up
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived pancreatic endoderm in a perforated open device; anti-thymocyte globulin induction with tacrolimus and mycophenolate maintenance
limitations: Small study; events are attributed as reported by the paper and do not establish comparative risk or causality beyond the authors' assessment
notes: The paper reports one serious event attributed to the surgical procedure and one to protocol-specified immunosuppression.

claim: ClinicalTrials.gov lists the VC-01 Encaptra study as terminated for insufficient functional product engraftment
population_or_model: Adults with T1D in the VC-01 study
design: Official ClinicalTrials.gov registry and posted results
endpoint: Trial status and registry termination reason; planned Cohort 2 C-peptide endpoint
follow_up: Registry record last posted 2022-03-24; status verified 2022-02
cointerventions: Stem-cell-derived pancreatic endoderm in a closed immune-protective macroencapsulation device
limitations: Historical registry record; Cohort 2 was never enrolled and its efficacy endpoint has no data; termination reason does not establish a specific fibrosis or oxygenation mechanism
notes: The registry reports 19 actual enrolled in Cohort 1, 9 completed and 10 not completed; the intended Cohort 2 had zero participants.

claim: ClinicalTrials.gov lists the Sernova Cell Pouch study as active but not recruiting; its protocol requires systemic immunosuppression before donor-islet transplantation
population_or_model: Adults with T1D and hypoglycemia unawareness
endpoint: Trial status and registered device/islet transplantation protocol
follow_up: Record last posted 2026-02-25; status verified 2026-02
cointerventions: Prevascularized scaffold followed by allogeneic donor islet transplantation with systemic immunosuppression
limitations: No results section was posted in the queried registry record; protocol details are not evidence of benefit or current site availability
notes: The registry estimates enrollment of 17 and describes tissue prevascularization before transplantation.

claim: ClinicalTrials.gov lists the Encellin ENC-201-CED islet-device feasibility study as active but not recruiting with no results posted
population_or_model: Adults with T1D receiving primary human islet infusion
endpoint: Trial status and registered safety, containment, and fibrosis outcomes
follow_up: Record last posted 2026-03-11; status verified 2026-03
cointerventions: Macroencapsulated allogeneic primary human islets
limitations: Estimated enrollment of 10; registry protocol is not evidence of reported non-fibrotic engraftment or clinical efficacy
notes: The primary endpoint is device-related adverse events through Day 134; fibrosis/containment assessments are secondary outcomes after Day 120.

claim: Four of 10 participants in the optimized PEC-Direct study group met the primary endpoint of detectable meal-stimulated C-peptide at month 6
population_or_model: People with T1D and undetectable baseline C-peptide in an optimized-device study group
design: Interim open-label phase 1/2 report with one-year follow-up
endpoint: MMTT-stimulated C-peptide above the assay limit of detection (0.03 nmol/L) at month 6 (primary endpoint)
follow_up: Month 6; follow-up to month 12 and beyond reported
cointerventions: Allogeneic stem-cell-derived pancreatic endoderm in a perforated open device; anti-thymocyte globulin induction with tacrolimus and mycophenolate maintenance
limitations: Small uncontrolled group; detectable C-peptide is a low threshold and is not insulin independence; the group is within NCT03163511 and is not an independent trial; authors disclose ViaCyte employment or advisory roles
notes: Three of these four participants also reached C-peptide >=0.1 nmol/L (EV-015) so the two outcomes are nested and must not be added; month-3 detectable C-peptide was reported in 5 of 10.

claim: Edited human hypoimmune (HLA class I/II-negative, CD47-overexpressing) primary islet pseudoislets survived, engrafted, and ameliorated diabetes in immunocompetent allogeneic diabetic humanized mice and avoided autoimmune killing in autologous diabetic humanized autoimmune mice
population_or_model: Diabetic allogeneic and autoimmune humanized mouse models
endpoint: Graft survival and engraftment; diabetes amelioration; avoidance of alloimmune and autoimmune killing
follow_up: Not stated in the accessible abstract
cointerventions: No immunosuppression required in the models as described
limitations: Mouse models only; sample sizes, observation durations, and per-endpoint denominators were not available because the full text was not accessible; authors are Sana-affiliated; does not establish human efficacy or safety
notes: Abstract also reports that unedited or partially edited contaminating cells did not impair survival or function of the edited pseudoislets; this is a model observation, not a product-purity standard.

claim: In the humanized mouse model, HIP pseudoislet cells were eliminated quickly and reliably using a CD47-targeting antibody, proposed by the authors as a safety strategy
population_or_model: Diabetic humanized mouse model with engrafted human HIP pseudoislets
endpoint: Elimination of HIP pseudoislet cells after anti-CD47 antibody treatment
follow_up: Not stated in the accessible abstract
cointerventions: Anti-CD47 antibody treatment
limitations: Preclinical single-model result; sample size and timing are not available from the abstract; no human data; whether an anti-CD47 approach would be effective, complete, selective, or safe for human cell removal is not established; off-target effects on other CD47-expressing cells were not assessed in the accessible record
notes: The authors frame this as a safety strategy in case HIP cells exert toxicity in a future clinical setting; it is a proposal supported by mouse data, not a validated clinical removal mechanism.
